# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

content.text: Starting Chapter 18 (Pirate Ship, "Survive"); the game is on the Preparations screen. Next I'm checking which units are deployed.
The army is badly underleveled (Eliwood Lv3, Rebecca Lv2) and has no healer. I'm reviewing stats and equipment before I pick the deployment.
ACTION t0 Deploy: swapping Erk (Lv2, Mag 5) for Canas (Mag 11, Flux) to get real magic damage.
Scouting the ship map before the battle; one Black Fang unit is already on board.
Still scouting: there are enemy pegasus knights over the water and shamans on the west ship. Checking the north and east next.
Map scouted (our ship in the middle, enemy ships on both sides). Returning to Preparations to swap Matthew out for Wil, since bows are good against the enemy pegasi.
ACTION t0 Deploy: Matthew is carrying no weapon at all, so he sits out and Wil comes in as a second bow for the pegasus knights.
ACTION t0 Deploy: the cursor slipped and picked Kent instead of Wil. I'm keeping him: a Lv6 cavalier with a Steel sword, a Javelin and a Vulnerary is a sturdier pick than a second archer.
ACTION t0 Merlinus: Yes. With no healer, mid-battle access to the convoy is worth having; I'll keep him walled in at the bow.
The battle has started; I'm reading through the opening dialogue (Fargus's crew says there's a shop on board).
Turn 1 (Survive 11 turns). I'm mapping enemy threat ranges before moving anyone.
Still reading the board: a sword unit on the east ship can cross the plank onto our deck. Checking its stats.

content.thinking: I'm planning to survive 11 turns: Lyn takes out the lone shaman on deck while Marcus walls off the east plank against the mercenary, and the rest stay bunched out of range. Lyn's Mani Katti should kill the shaman in one clean strike.

Lyn has taken out the shaman, so I'm moving Marcus onto the deck tile at the east plank's mouth to block it. He should hold there, since the mercenary can only reach him from the plank and his counters should finish it off.

content.text: Moving Hector to (7,7) to shield Lyn's north side.
ACTION t1 Hector: Hand axe equipped instead of the Devil axe, which has about a 25% chance to backfire with his Luck of 6. He waits at (7,7), screening Lyn's north side.
ACTION t1 Kent: wait at (8,7) beside Lyn, so the only open sides she has are the stairs and the west.
ACTION t1 Sain: wait at (6,6) beside Hector. The tile west of Lyn turned out not to be walkable, which already closes that side.
Found it: the green cabin door is an Armory. Opening it with Eliwood to see stock and gold.
0 gold, so nothing to buy. Backing out.
ACTION t1 Oswin: step down beside Marcus at the east plank as a second wall; with Def 17 the mercenary can't hurt him.

content.thinking: Lyn has taken the kill, with Marcus and Oswin holding the east plank and Hector and Kent boxing her in, while Eliwood's group waits idle in the bow. I expect the mercenary to charge Marcus and the pegasi to close from the south.

content.text: Turn 2. The mercenary never attacked; it fell back. Two pegasus knights are now close, one on the west plank and one over the east channel. Checking their reach.
The pegasi are fragile (17 HP, Def 4), and Sain's Steel lance does exactly 17. Moving to one-shot the west one.

content.thinking: I picked Kent over Sain, since the cavaliers look alike, so Kent attacks with a Steel sword for 10 at 94% hit. That leaves the pegasus at 7 for a follow-up kill, though Kent may take about 7 damage back.

content.text: Kent killed the west pegasus (now 17/25 HP). Next: get Lyn healed; she's at 12/22.
Lyn has no vulnerary, only a Red Gem. Backing out to walk her next to Canas, who carries two.
Lyn now holds Canas's Vulnerary. Using it.
ACTION t2 Lyn: drink the Vulnerary (+10, back to 22/22) beside Canas in the bow.
Lyn is healed. Kent is the problem: he's still out on the west plank at 17 HP, within reach of the west-ship shamans and a pegasus. Planning to have Sain rescue him and ride back.
ACTION t2 Sain: Rescue Kent off the plank; then use his leftover move to ride back toward the middle of the deck, away from the shamans' range.
Kent is safe, carried by Sain. Next, Marcus rides to the lower east plank to kill the east pegasus; Iron sword does 19 against its 17 HP.
ACTION t2 Marcus: Iron sword on the east pegasus, 18 damage at 100% hit against 17 HP; dead on the first swing.
Pegasus down. Next, Oswin slides over to plug the upper east plank that Marcus left.
ACTION t2 Oswin: hold the upper east plank mouth. Nothing on the east ship can hurt Def 17.

content.thinking: Two pegasi are down, with Oswin on the upper east plank and Marcus on the lower one. I'm moving Hector onto the deck stairs, where the shaman started, to block a possible reinforcement spawn.

content.text: ACTION t2 Hector: stand on the deck stairs (5,6) to plug the likely spawn point. With Def 13 and a Hand axe for counters, he's the right body for it.

content.thinking: Kent and Marcus each downed a pegasus, Sain pulled Kent back, Lyn healed, and Oswin and Marcus are holding the two east planks while Hector guards the stairs. I expect the last pegasus and perhaps the archer to press Marcus next.

Marcus downed a Lancereaver and another pegasus on the enemy phase, leaving him at 33/36. The Steel-sword mercenary and archer are now lined up against Oswin on the upper plank, so I'm checking their HP.

content.text: The Steel-sword mercenary is down to 2/21 after Oswin's counters, with a full-HP archer behind it. Canas will finish the mercenary with Flux from two tiles away.

content.thinking: Clearing the upper east plank now: Canas is attacking the 2-HP Longsword unit from range 2 with an 87% hit chance, while Oswin holds the plank mouth and Marcus keeps the lower plank.

content.text: Canas killed it. Checking the archer's stats to see whether Oswin can finish it from the plank.
The archer is weak (Str 5, Def 4, 20 HP); good EXP fodder. Seeing who can reach it.
ACTION t3 Oswin: step onto the plank and lance the archer. 19×2 at 98% hit against 20 HP; the Steel bow slows it enough for Oswin to double, and it can't counter at range 1.
Oswin killed the archer and leveled up (37 HP). Checking the south half before moving the rest.
A west-ship shaman is walking across the west plank toward us. Hector can Hand axe it from two tiles away.
ACTION t3 Hector: Hand axe on the shaman from two tiles. 17 damage against 18 HP leaves it at 1, which a weak unit can finish for EXP; it hits back for 9 at 70%.
Hector is at 20/29 and the shaman is at 1 HP. Sain (still carrying Kent) will try to finish it.
ACTION t3 Sain: Steel lance on the 1-HP shaman while still carrying Kent. 72% displayed, about 79% real; a miss costs about 10 HP on the counter.
Sain killed the shaman and picked up a Guiding Ring (the promotion item for Canas once he hits Lv10).

content.thinking: Canas, Oswin and Sain each scored a kill and Hector chipped in, while Lyn, Eliwood, Rebecca, Bartre and Guy hold the bow. I expect the west-ship shaman to hit Hector or Sain for about 9 damage, and the east-ship fighters to engage Oswin and Marcus.

content.text: Turn 4. Oswin killed an Armorslayer mercenary on the enemy phase (now 34/37). A second shaman has moved up next to Sain and Hector on the west plank. Checking HP.
Sain is down to 9/23 and needs to get off the plank. Checking the shaman.

content.thinking: Only Hector and Sain can reach the shaman, and a Sain miss could kill him on the counter at 9 HP. I'm pulling both back toward the ship, with Lyn moving first so Hector can take a Vulnerary from her.

content.text: ACTION t4 Lyn: wait at (8,5), just outside the shaman's reach, so Hector can step beside her and take a Vulnerary.
Hector has the Vulnerary. Drinking it now (20 → 29 HP).
ACTION t4 Hector: drink the Vulnerary at (7,5), from 20 back toward full, before the shamans arrive.
Hector is back to 29/29. Now Sain, at 9 HP and still carrying Kent, retreats.

content.thinking: Sain stopped at (8,4) still holding Kent, and a press hit Wait rather than Drop, both out of the shaman's reach, so I'm leaving them. Next I'll move the bow group to mid-deck so they can take kills next turn.

Hector is healed to full at (7,5) as bait for the shaman, with Lyn beside him, while Sain and Kent pull back and Oswin and Marcus hold the east planks. The bow group stays idle on purpose, and I expect the shaman to Flux Hector for about 8.

content.text: Turn 5. Quiet enemy phase: nobody was hit, and the shamans pulled back to the west ship (two now sit at its edge). Scanning for new arrivals.
East ship looks empty now. I'll use the lull to have Hector hand Kent off Sain so Sain can take Kent's Vulnerary, and have Lyn sell her Red Gem at the Armory for weapons.
ACTION t5 Hector: took Kent from Sain and is dropping him at (3,7), so Sain can grab Kent's Vulnerary.
At the Armory with Lyn. Selling her Red Gem for gold, then buying weapons.
ACTION t5 Lyn: selling the Red Gem for 2500 G, enough to restock weapons before the Dread Isle, where there are no shops.
Sold for 2500 G. Checking the full buy list.
ACTION t5 Lyn: buying a Hand axe (300 G) for Hector, whose current one has 5 uses left.
Bought. Next: Steel axe (360 G) as Hector's main weapon.
ACTION t5 Lyn: Steel axe bought (1840 G left). Now a Javelin (400 G) so Oswin can hit at 1–2 range.
ACTION t5 Lyn: Javelin bought (1440 G left). Last purchase: a Steel lance (480 G) as Oswin's backup, since his Iron lance has 16 uses. That leaves 960 G banked.
Lyn finished shopping: Hand axe, Steel axe, Javelin and Steel lance, with 960 G left. Now Sain steps next to Kent, takes his Vulnerary and drinks it.
ACTION t5 Sain: drink Kent's Vulnerary (9 → 19 HP).
Sain's Vulnerary went through. The game then offered his leftover mounted move; he's ending in place.
Sain is at 19/23. Next, Canas reads his Secret Book (a permanent stat boost) since nothing is in range.
ACTION t5 Canas: read the Secret Book for a permanent Skill boost.
Canas has read the book. Everyone else holds, so I'm ending turn 5.

content.thinking: This turn was a quiet logistics pass: weapons bought, Sain healed, Kent dealt with, and Canas occupied with his book. Oswin and Marcus will hold the east planks while the bow group stays idle, and I expect the shamans to remain on their ship unless provoked.

content.text: Turn 6. Two shamans have crossed onto the west plank right next to our deck. Checking their HP before going in.
Both shamans are at 18/18. Lyn walks over to hand Hector his new Steel axe and Hand axe.
Trading weapons from Lyn to Hector: the Steel axe goes into his empty slot.
Hector now has a Steel axe and a fresh Hand axe. Lyn waits.
Next, Hector attacks the right-hand shaman with the new Steel axe.

content.thinking: Turn 6 is set: both shamans fall at the west plank mouth, Hector opening with the Steel axe. Hector's strike has an 82% chance to one-shot the near shaman.

content.text: Hector one-shot the first shaman and took no damage. Kent goes for the second; Steel sword ×2 should do it.
ACTION t6 Kent: Steel sword on the second shaman, 11×2 at 90% for 22 against 18 HP. Its counter does 10 at 67%, so Kent (17 HP) survives even the worst case.
Kent got the kill but is down to 7/25 at the plank mouth. Checking what's left on the west ship before deciding how to cover him.
That last unit's reach stays on its own ship, so Kent isn't threatened by it. Still, at 7 HP he shouldn't be left out front: Sain will rescue him and ride back.
ACTION t6 Sain: Rescue Kent (7 HP) and carry him back off the plank mouth; one pegasus hit would kill him.
Kent is tucked away on Sain. Everyone else holds, so I'm ending turn 6.

content.thinking: Both western shamans, Hector and Kent, are down, and Sain is carrying the wounded Kent. Only one stationary unit remains on the west ship, so I expect a quiet phase unless reinforcements appear.

content.text: Turn 7, and the enemy phase was quiet again. Sweeping the map for reinforcements.
North is clear. Lyn walks over to Oswin to hand off the Javelin, Steel lance and Horseslayer.
